---
title: Read a calendar
description: List the events that fall in a window of time, with each recurring event unfolded into one entry for each time it happens.
job: A builder lists the events in a time window with each recurring event unfolded.
---

A recurring calendar [event](/catalog/event), a `core.event` item and not an [event-stream](/build/events) event, is one item with a `recurrence` rule, so a listing can't say what happens on a given day. [List event occurrences](/reference/api/items/listOccurrences) can: Marfa works out each time an event happens when you ask. In the TypeScript example, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows.

## List a window

Name the start and end of the window:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items occurrences --from 2026-12-01 --to 2026-12-15
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /occurrences?from=2026-12-01&to=2026-12-15
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/occurrences", {
  params: { query: { from: "2026-12-01", to: "2026-12-15" } },
});
```

Each entry in `data` has a `starts_at`, an `ends_at` where the event has a length, and the whole `item`, in order of `starts_at`. An occurrence of a recurring event carries a `series_id`, the `id` of the event whose rule made it. **The whole window comes in one page**, and `window` says what was read, in UTC. A window holds:

- **Every active event that overlaps it**, including one already running when it opens. Archived events and events in the bin are left out.
- **Events only.** A task can carry a `recurrence` rule too, but the listing never answers tasks.
- **Only the types the credential can read.** `type` narrows it to one event type and the types under it.

## Show a moved occurrence

When one occurrence moves, such as a class pushed back a day, the move is its own event. It holds `original_starts_at`, and the series points to it by a `parent-of` [edge](/build/edges). The listing shows it at its own times and nothing at the old slot. When the credential can read the series and the edge, the entry also carries the `series_id` and, in `replaces`, the start it took over.

## Write the bounds

`from` and `to` are each a date-time with a zone and seconds, such as `2026-12-01T09:00:00+01:00`, or a date with no time, which is its midnight in UTC. Marfa refuses with `400 validation_error` a bound in any other form, a date that doesn't exist, a `to` that isn't after its `from`, a window over 400 days, and one that holds more than 5,000 occurrences. It never sends a trimmed answer: narrow the window.

## Check the calendar is whole

A series that takes too long to unfold, or has more than 2,000 occurrences in the window, is left out, and the rest still answers. When that happens the answer carries **`expansion_incomplete: true`**, and `scan.series_unexpanded` counts the series left out. Show the person that the calendar is incomplete rather than present it as whole.

The rules are in the [occurrences](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/occurrences.md) chapter of the contract.
